title: OneCall surface PRD + Canary Rollout Sanity Checklist for Hosted Generation + Embeddings
creator: Priya Shah
description: Deliver a compact PRD that defines the OneCall surface: a single unified hosted API route that supports generation (chat/completions), embeddings, and rerank as first-class behaviors with deterministic behavior, throttling and graceful fallbacks. Include a practical canary rollout plan and an operational sanity checklist to validate latency, correctness, and cost metrics during staggered ramp.
requirements: Expose a single endpoint /v1/onecall that accepts a 1MB max JSON payload and a 'mode' field (chat | completion | embedding | rerank).
Backward-compatible SDK adapters in JS/Python that map existing chat/completions/embeddings calls to OneCall with minimal code changes.
Routing policy: prefer lowest-latency model for mode=chat/completion; fallback to quantized variant on capacity pressure; embeddings must route to embedding-optimized model.
Rate limits and per-customer concurrency caps configurable via tenant config; default soft limit 60 reqs/min and burst to 200 for 15s.
Streaming support for chat/completion with chunked SSE/grpc equivalent; embeddings and rerank return non-streaming JSON payloads.
Structured output v1: must support a `response.metadata` block with model, latency_ms, quantization_flag, and routed_node_id.
Telemetry: emit tokenized cost estimate, token_count, latency_p95, and quality-guard metrics for each request into BigQuery/Telemetry pipeline.
Security: requests must pass tenant auth; OneCall must respect per-tenant KMS keys for any optional output encryption at rest for temporary artifacts.
Operational: expose per-route dashboards and a healthcheck that returns per-backend capacity score and kv-cache hit rate.
Acceptance criteria must be automatable where applicable and tied to observability dashboards for rollout gating.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: OneCall responds correctly to equivalent existing chat/completions/embeddings/rerank payloads used in the migration test harness (test-suite v2.1) within 2% semantic parity for sampled prompts.
Performance: Cold-start median latency for chat (seq_len=128) < 160ms on dedicated lane; p95 < 450ms. Embedding latency p95 < 250ms.

Throughput & cost: For a synthetic mixed workload (60% chat, 30% embeddings, 10% rerank), system sustains 250 reqs/s on the dedicated pool with simulated KV cache enabled, and unit token cost meets or improves on current baseline by >=10%.
Reliability: Canary sustain for 48h with error rate <0.5% and no SLO violations in error budget window for connected tenants.
Observability: Dashboards surface token-level cost and route breakdowns; alerts configured for latency/p95 regression, kv-cache drop >10 percentage points, or route misrouting incidents.
Compatibility: Official JS and Python adapter libs pass the compatibility smoke tests and produce identical typed responses (schema validation) for 1000 historical requests.
Security: SSO/KMS integration test passes; audit logs record per-request routing decisions and KMS key usage when encryption is enabled.
Docs: Public PRD, Quickstart, and migration guide published to Confluence and docs.redwood.ai; example migration PRs exist in internal monorepo.
scope_changes: Initial scope included support for multimodal binary payloads — deferred to M2 to reduce launch risk (modes limited to text-based use cases).
Support for fine-grained tenant routing rules (custom model selection) postponed; default routing policies will be opinionated for launch.
On-device quantized model catalog integration (private on-prem variant) scoped out of the hosted beta.

notes: Prefer an opinionated default routing map (chat->gpt-small-lowlat, embeddings->embed-fast) to reduce customer configuration complexity.
We will publish a migration linting tool that flags incompatible fields when swapping callers to OneCall from legacy endpoints.
Risk: combining many behaviors into a single route increases attack surface for schema misuse — mitigations include strict schema validation, per-tenant quotas, and early error responses.
